Named notice 21943329: 14 shuffled lots. The five listed moves are served as listed: RES-1->LOT-2 (prints 14), RES-2->LOT-7 (12), RES-3->LOT-9 (11), RES-4->LOT-4 (2), RES-7->LOT-6 (10). RES-5->LOT-13 (8), RES-6->LOT-1 (1), RES-8->LOT-12 (4) and RES-9->LOT-11 (6) are exact.

Named notice 23074890 (34 blocks, 22 shuffled lots): all 12 listed moves are served as listed. RES-7, RES-24 and RES-26 (LOT_NO 15) are on LOT-3; RES-9, RES-20 and RES-31 (21) on LOT-5. Also RES-10->LOT-6 (12), RES-11->LOT-7 (17), RES-13->LOT-9 (13), RES-17->LOT-20 (1), RES-19->LOT-22 (14) and RES-23->LOT-12 (10). The rule leaves those on no lot, and all ten are served on none. Named notice 23256169: lots print 1-6,8,11,13,14,15,16. The listed move RES-8 (LOT_NO 11) is served on LOT-8. The other 11 blocks are on their exact LOT_NO lots.
Named notice 23319363: lots print 2,3,1. The listed move RES-2 (LOT_NO 1) is served on LOT-3. RES-1 (2) is on LOT-1 and RES-3 (3) on LOT-2, both correct.

Named notice 23413021: lots print 01,03,04,05,06,08,10..17. The listed moves RES-7 (LOT_NO 10) -> LOT-7, RES-8 (11) -> LOT-8 and RES-9 (12) -> LOT-9 are served. The other 11 blocks are exact. The second award notice 23276289 has a single lot section, LOT-1, printing '02' (terrassement), and its RES-1 (LOT_NO 02) is served on LOT-1, which the rule requires. Outside 567's rule: lots are keyed by the section ids of each award notice, so this block lands on the tender lot keyed LOT-1, which the tender titles 'v.r.d' (lot 01 of the named notice). That is a separate cross-notice keying question, not a 567 misplacement.

fresh_reader.why: Award notice 21742060 (F03 R2.0.9, 299440-2021) has 44 lot sections. Each prints a scrambled LOT_NO that is not its ITEM (LOT-1=42, LOT-11=4, LOT-26=1, LOT-44=2 ...), and no number appears twice. All 40 award blocks carry a LOT_NO, each matching exactly one lot section, and the served lot is that section in 40 of 40 (e.g. RES-1 LOT_NO 44 -> LOT-20, RES-13 LOT_NO 1 -> LOT-26, RES-28 LOT_NO 2 -> LOT-44). Under the old first-claim rule 22 blocks sat on the lot at their ordinal (e.g. RES-13 on LOT-1); 567 moved them. Block titles match the Tender's lot titles 32/32 where a title is present.

Award notice 22532830 (F03, 353381-2022): lots LOT-1..LOT-5 print LOT_NO 1..5. The blocks print LOT_NO '01'..'05', so nothing matches exactly, and each has exactly one normalised match. Served RES-k -> LOT-k for all 5. Before 567 all 5 blocks were on no lot (the '0k' LOT_NO missed and was the last reference). They moved none -> lot through the normalised number, as the rule allows. Block titles agree with the lot titles.

Award notice 21858408 (F03, 402053-2021): lots print LOT_NO 1 and 2; the blocks print '01' and '02'. Each has one normalised match, so RES-1 -> LOT-1 and RES-2 -> LOT-2, and both are served there. Before 567 both were on no lot. This is the normalised-number class (none -> lot), consistent with the rule.

Award notice 20472047 (F03, 279547-2019): LOT-1 prints 3, LOT-2 prints 2, LOT-3 prints 1 (rotated numbering). RES-1 has LOT_NO 3, goes to LOT-1 and is served there. RES-2 has LOT_NO 1, goes to LOT-3 and is served there. RES-2 was on LOT-1 before 567, a misattribution, and moved to LOT-3. Block titles ('Echipament pentru recuperarea mersului', 'Aparate fizioterapie') match the served lots' titles.

Award notice 22510410 (F03, 411504-2022): 11 lots with scrambled LOT_NOs (LOT-1=11, LOT-10=1, LOT-9=2 ...). All 11 blocks match their LOT_NO exactly and are served on that section (e.g. RES-1 LOT_NO 4 -> LOT-7, RES-9 LOT_NO 1 -> LOT-10, RES-10 LOT_NO 11 -> LOT-1). Five moved from the old wrong lot (RES-1 LOT-4->7, RES-2 LOT-6->8, RES-3 LOT-2->9, RES-7 LOT-10->6, RES-9 LOT-1->10). The other version notices are a contract notice and four F14 corrigenda; none has an award block.

There are two award notices, each with one lot section and one block that prints no number (ITEM 1 only). In 22568917 (437227-2022) the lot LOT-1 prints LOT_NO 1 and ITEM 1, so every lot's number is its ordinal and RES-1 goes to LOT-1, as served (title 'Spraugas lampa...' matches). In 22583013 (432061-2022) the lot LOT-1 prints LOT_NO 2 but ITEM 1, so the no-number block goes on no lot, and it is served on none. Before 567 that block sat on Tender LOT-1 'Spraugas lampa', the wrong lot; its title 'Oftalmologa darba vietas aprikojuma komplekts' is the Tender's LOT-2. 567 moved it off the wrong lot. The rule cannot put it on LOT-2 because the block prints no number.

There are 12 award notices (F03, 570950-2021 through 716891-2023), and all 540 blocks match the rule. Every notice and the contract notice print the same 12-lot numbering, which is not the ordinals (LOT-1=8, LOT-2=10, LOT-8=2, LOT-11=1 ...), so lot keys are consistent across notices. 512 blocks match their LOT_NO exactly and are served on that section. The other 28 print LOT_NO '2,1', which no lot section prints, even normalised, so the rule puts them on no lot, and all 28 are served on none. They were on none before 567 too. 344 blocks moved from the old ordinal lot to the LOT_NO lot (e.g. LOT-11->LOT-7 x14, LOT-6->LOT-9 x13, LOT-10->LOT-2 x11). Block titles match the Tender lot titles in 484 blocks; 8 differ only by a truncated title.

Award notice 19666745 (F15, 052721-2018) has one lot section, LOT-1, which prints LOT_NO 2 and ITEM 1. The block prints only ITEM 1, and the lot's number is not its ordinal, so the rule puts the block on no lot; it is served lot null. Before 567 it was on LOT-1. Caveat: this is the Tender's only lot, and the block title equals that lot's title ('14-0481 Electricite courants forts... Lot no 2'). The old placement was arguably correct, and the rule's no-number clause now drops it to the Tender. That is what the rule says, but it loses information in this case.

155 blocks in 12 award notices, and every one is on the section of its own notice that the rule picks. 18911154 (R2.0.8 form 3) has no lot sections, so its two LOT_NUMBER blocks are on none, as served. In 8 notices (19786640-20827122, 2018-2020) LOT-1 prints LOT_NO 2 ('Kojenecka voda') and LOT-2 prints LOT_NO 1 ('Lahve a savicky'). There the LOT_NO 1 blocks are served on LOT-2 and the LOT_NO 2 blocks on LOT-1, both matching exactly. 20827122 RES-18 prints no number and the lots are not ordinal, so it is on none, as served. In the 3 notices from 2020 the lots print 1/2 in order and blocks are served on LOT-1/LOT-2. 120 blocks moved LOT-1 -> LOT-2. FINDING OUTSIDE 567: the Tender merges lots by section id across notices, but section ids mean different lots in different notices. The Tender's lots[] (v13, from notice 21337435) say LOT-1 = 'Lahve a savicky' and LOT-2 = 'Kojenecka voda'. So 147 blocks from 2018-2020 (120 titled 'Lahve a savicky' on LOT-2, 27 titled 'Kojenecka voda' on LOT-1) now sit on the Tender lot with the other title. Before 567 the 120 Lahve blocks happened to sit on LOT-1, which matches their title. The rule is met per notice, but cross-notice lot-key identity needs its own issue.

Award notice 20458615 (F03, 268151-2019) has 4 lots: LOT-1 prints 2, LOT-2 prints 1 (swapped), LOT-3 and LOT-4 print 3 and 4. Its one block RES-1 prints only ITEM 1 and no number. Not every lot's number is its ordinal, so the rule puts it on no lot; it is served lot null. Before 567 it was on LOT-1, which is lot number 2, so this is a to-none correction consistent with the rule. The block has no title to cross-check.

One award notice, 20334631 (F06). Its lot sections print the numbers 1 and 2, which equal their ordinals. The blocks print LOT_NO 'Lot 1' (RES-1..3) and 'Lot 2' (RES-4..5). No lot prints these exactly. Once normalised they match exactly one lot each, so all five blocks belong on LOT-1 and LOT-2, which is what the API serves. All 5 moved in 567, from no lot to their lot through the normalised match. The block titles agree with the lot titles.

One award notice, 23117767 (F03). It has 40 lot sections printing scrambled numbers. RES-1 prints LOT_NO 18, which only LOT-36 prints exactly, so it is on LOT-36. RES-5 prints 38, printed only by LOT-4, so it is on LOT-4. The other 8 blocks print comma lists such as '36,26' and '29,4,20,5'. No lot prints these, exactly or normalised, so they are on no lot and the API serves them on none. Two blocks moved in 567: RES-1 from LOT-18 to LOT-36 and RES-5 from LOT-38 to LOT-4.

Two award notices. In 19043870 the 7 blocks match the 7 lot numbers exactly, and none of them moved. In 19152735 there are 23 lot sections with skipped and rotated numbers. 16 blocks match exactly; for example RES-10 prints LOT_NO 1 and is on LOT-4. Three blocks ('14 и 15', '24, 25 и 30', '8 и 18') match no lot, so they are on none. Ten blocks moved in 567 to the lot their LOT_NO names, and the block titles agree. Outside the rule: 19043870's LOT-1..7 keys are its own ordinals, while the Tender's LOT-1..7 titles come from 19152735. Those 7 blocks therefore sit on Tender keys that carry another lot's title. This predates 567 and 567 did not change it.

One award notice, 21479224, with 46 lot sections printing scrambled but unique numbers. All 31 blocks match a lot number exactly and are served on that lot. 17 of them moved in 567; for example RES-18 (LOT_NO 10) went from LOT-10 to LOT-3, and RES-27 (LOT_NO 1) from LOT-1 to LOT-27. Block titles match the lot titles.

Two award notices. In 21927890 there are 7 lots printing 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 16 and 30; its 7 blocks match exactly and none moved. In 22001080 there are 23 lots and all 23 blocks match exactly. Four of those moved in 567 (RES-6..9 from LOT-11..14 to LOT-6..9), and their titles agree. Outside the rule: as with 8387180, 21927890's LOT-1..7 keys are its ordinals, while the Tender's LOT-1..7 titles come from 22001080. For example, the 'Zad.3' award sits on the Tender's LOT-1, which is titled 'Zad.1'. This predates 567 and is unchanged.

15 award notices, each with the same 101 lot sections. The printed numbers are rotated, not ordinals. They are unique within each notice and keep the same number on the same key in all 15 notices. 1010 blocks match exactly and are served on that lot. 54 blocks, all in 22224369 and 22364170, print comma lists such as '98,99' or '25,64' that match no lot, and they are served on none. 692 blocks moved in 567; for example RES-1 (LOT_NO 3) went from LOT-3 to LOT-37, the lot with the same title. The title differences between notices are whitespace only.

Notice 19545377 has 36 lots. LOT-1 and LOT-2 both print '1b', and LOT-9 and LOT-10 both print '1i'. So the 7 '1b' blocks and 5 '1i' blocks are on none, because two lots print the number. The '1a' and '1j' blocks match no lot and are on none. RES-136 prints '2L', which no lot prints exactly; normalised it matches only LOT-24 ('2l'), so it is on LOT-24. The other 148 blocks match exactly. Notice 20830825 is an F20 modification: its one lot prints '1, 2 and 3' and its block prints 'Lots 1, 2 and 3'. 'Lots' is not a prefix the normaliser drops, so that block is on none. Everything is served as the rule puts it. 13 blocks moved in 567: 12 from LOT-1 or LOT-10 to none (the duplicated numbers), and RES-136 from none to LOT-24.

Notice 20395099 has two lots with swapped numbers: LOT-1 prints 2 and LOT-2 prints 1. The blocks printing 1 (RES-1, 3, 5) are on LOT-2 and the blocks printing 2 are on LOT-1. Titles confirm it ('centre copii' blocks are on the 'copii' lot). RES-1, 3 and 5 moved in 567 from LOT-1 to LOT-2. Notice 20798220 has one lot section that prints no number, so lots are keyed by ordinal and its ITEM-only block RES-1 goes to LOT-1, as served. That block did not move.

Notice 21687822 has one lot section with ITEM 1 that prints LOT_NO 2. The single block RES-1 prints only ITEM 1. The rule places a block with no number by its ordinal only where every lot's number is its ordinal. Here 2 is not 1, so the block is on none, and the API serves lot null. It moved in 567 from LOT-1 to none. This is correct by the rule, but note the cost: the only award of a one-lot Tender now sits on the Tender, not the lot.

Notice 20493982 has 4 lots with reversed numbering: LOT-1 to LOT-4 print 4, 3, 2 and 1. RES-1 to RES-4 print LOT_NO 4, 3, 2 and 1, so each matches its lot exactly and is served there. Two blocks moved in 567: RES-3 from LOT-2 to LOT-3 and RES-4 from LOT-1 to LOT-4.

Award notice 20709957 (489531-2019). Two lot sections print LOT_NO, and neither number is the section's ordinal: LOT-1 is ITEM 1 / LOT_NO 2 and LOT-2 is ITEM 2 / LOT_NO 3. RES-1 and RES-2 print only ITEM 1 and ITEM 2, with no LOT_NO or LOT_NUMBER. Under the rule, a block with no number goes on its ITEM ordinal only when every lot section's number is its ordinal, which is not the case here, so both go on none. The API serves RES-1 and RES-2 with lot null. Before 567 both sat on LOT-1, because the first-claim map gave ITEM 2 to LOT-1 through LOT-1's LOT_NO 2. The award titles (Papeterie, Supports) point at LOT-1 and LOT-2, but the rule does not read titles.

Award notice 22692214 (542129-2022). The lot sections print swapped numbers: LOT-1 prints 2 ('Lotul 2'), LOT-2 prints 1 ('Lotul 1'), LOT-3 prints 3. Each block matches its LOT_NO exactly: RES-1 (LOT_NO 1) goes to LOT-2, RES-2 (LOT_NO 2) to LOT-1, RES-3 (LOT_NO 3) to LOT-3. The API serves exactly these. RES-1 moved from LOT-1 to LOT-2.

Award notice 22963000 (073356-2023). The two lot sections print LOT_NO '1.34.7/2020/1' and '1.34.7/2020/2'. The five blocks print LOT_NO 1, 2, 1, 1, 2 (ITEMs 1 to 5). None of these numbers matches a lot section's printed number, either exactly or after normalising, so the rule leaves all five on the Tender (none). The API serves all five with lot null. Before 567 the bare LOT_NO hit the ITEM keys, putting RES-1, RES-3 and RES-4 on LOT-1 and RES-2 and RES-5 on LOT-2. All five moved to none, as the rule says ('a number no lot publishes leaves the award on the Tender').

Award notice 19048669 (460763-2016). Swapped numbering: LOT-1 prints 2 ('Lot 2: NHH fixed') and LOT-2 prints 1 ('Lot 1: HH flexible'). RES-1 (LOT_NO 2) matches LOT-1 exactly and RES-2 (LOT_NO 1) matches LOT-2 exactly. The API serves both as the rule says, and the award titles agree. RES-2 moved from LOT-1 to LOT-2.

Award notice 20524440 (332231-2019). There are 24 lot sections. Sections 1 to 20 print their own ordinal; the last four rotate: LOT-21 prints 22, LOT-22 prints 23, LOT-23 prints 24, LOT-24 prints 21. Each of the 24 blocks matches its LOT_NO exactly, including RES-24 (LOT_NO 21) going to LOT-24. The API serves all 24 as the rule says, and every award title agrees with its lot. RES-24 moved from LOT-21 to LOT-24.

Award notice 21129364 (317155-2020). The four lot sections print LOT_NO 2, 4, 3, 1, so their numbers are not their ordinals. The only block, RES-1, prints just ITEM 1 and no number, which under the rule puts it on none. The API serves RES-1 with lot null. Before 567 it was on LOT-1.

Award notice 20582272 (374597-2019). The lot sections print 1 and 2. The blocks print LOT_NO '01' and '02'. Neither matches exactly; after normalising, each matches one lot: RES-1 goes to LOT-1 and RES-2 to LOT-2. The API serves both as the rule says. Before 567 both were on none, so this is the 'gains a lot where only the normalised number matched' case. Side note, not a rule question: the publisher's award titles look crossed against the lot titles (RES-1 'solutions de contrôle' vs LOT-1 'réactifs'). The rule follows LOT_NO, not titles.

Four award notices: 22985422 (104 blocks), 23006386 (117), 23082943 (128) and 23303960 (134). All four carry the same 122 lot sections, 121 of which print a number that is not their ordinal (for example LOT-1 prints 39, LOT-6 prints 12, LOT-11 prints 2). No number is printed twice. 412 blocks match their LOT_NO exactly, and the API serves each on that lot. 71 blocks carry a list of numbers as their LOT_NO (for example '12,100,14' or '7,9'). No lot prints such a list, so the rule puts those on none, and the API serves them with lot null. The API has no lot_result without a matching block. 208 blocks moved, all onto the lot their LOT_NO names (for example RES-10 of 22985422 from LOT-113 to LOT-19).

Award notice 19058375 (422679-2016). Seven lot sections; LOT-1 prints 2 and LOT-2 prints 1, and LOT-3 to LOT-7 print their own ordinal. The six blocks carry LOT_NO 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, and the API serves them exactly as the rule says: RES-1 on LOT-2, RES-2 on LOT-1, RES-3 on LOT-3, RES-4 on LOT-4, RES-5 on LOT-6, RES-6 on LOT-7. The award titles agree. Lot 5 has no award. RES-1 moved from LOT-1 to LOT-2.

Five award notices: 21317712, 21323853, 21469187, 22140760 and 22256951. In each, LOT-1 prints 2 ('Lot 2 ACI Nădlac') and LOT-2 prints 1 ('Lot 1 ... Sediul Central'). In every notice RES-1 has LOT_NO 2 and goes to LOT-1; every other block has LOT_NO 1 and goes to LOT-2. All 20 blocks are served exactly as the rule says, and the award titles naming 'Lot 1' agree. 15 blocks moved from LOT-1 to LOT-2. The lot titles in the earlier notices are worded differently ('doi ani' instead of '2 ani'), but every notice has the same numbering.

Agree. Award notice 22568917: its one lot prints LOT_NO 1 with ITEM 1, so every lot's number is its ordinal. Its block prints no number (ITEM 1 only), goes to LOT-1 and is served there. LOT-11=1), with no repeats. 512 blocks have one exact LOT_NO match and are served on it.
